function: CNN maps channel matrices (BS-RIS, RIS-UE, direct) to discrete 2-bit RIS phase shifts that maximize MIMO channel capacity (p. 1-3).
system: Reflecting RIS with 256 elements (sizes 4 to 256, 2-bit), 64-element planar BS array, 64-element planar UE array, direct plus RIS path, 28 GHz indoor office (p. 2).
method: End-to-end CNN (Conv2D, global pooling, dense head), trained unsupervised with Gumbel-Softmax relaxation and a negative-capacity loss; hard arg-max at inference (p. 3).
data_channel: SimRIS (3D 5G mmWave, 3GPP-compliant path loss and beamforming), indoor office; 10,000 snapshots split 60/20/20; UMi street canyon and NLOS scenarios also tested (p. 2-3).
test_conditions: Trained on indoor-office snapshots (60/20/20 split); tested on held-out snapshots and, claimed without retraining, UMi outdoor and NLOS; RIS-size sweep 4 to 256, retraining not stated (p. 2-4).
baselines: Non-learned: AGA (refs. 12-13) and WaOA (ref. 14) metaheuristics. Learned: DRL (ref. 6), GNN (ref. 8); MLP ablation (p. 3-4).
metrics: Mean achievable capacity (bps/Hz), execution/inference time, standard deviation and 95% confidence intervals over Monte Carlo runs, FLOPs and parameter count (p. 3-4).
complexity: About 28 million FLOPs per forward pass, 35,552 trainable parameters (139KB), measured inference latency 28 ms, CPU-only laptop (p. 1, 3).
openness: Code on GitHub: https://github.com/Kinza232/GumbleRIS (p. 3, ref. 15 on p. 5); channel simulator SimRIS is public (p. 2).
q1_support: p. 2: "3GPP-compliant path loss and beamforming models" - the public SimRIS simulator (5G mmWave, indoor office, Table I) also gives the "3GPP-compliant UMi Outdoor Street Canyon" (p. 3); TR 38.901 is not named, flagged in notes.
q2_support: p. 3: "evaluated in both a 3GPP-compliant UMi Outdoor Street Canyon and a strict NLOS scenario" after training on the indoor office layout (p. 2); p. 2: "generalizes robustly without retraining". The training data of the outdoor and NLOS tests are not described.
q3_support: p. 3: "Metaheuristics - AGA [12], [13] and WaOA [14], deep learning algorithms - DRL [6] and GNN [8]" - all compared on capacity (Fig. 2, Table II, p. 4).
q4_support: p. 3: "approximately 28 million FLOPs per forward pass" and "35,552 trainable parameters"; inference latency is measured and plotted as execution time (p. 3, Fig. 2 on p. 4).
q5_support: p. 3: "The codes used in this letter are available on GitHub" - link in ref. [15] on p. 5: https://github.com/Kinza232/GumbleRIS.
notes: Area 3, RIS phase configuration. Please confirm q1: SimRIS is a public simulator that the paper calls 3GPP-compliant (path loss, beamforming, UMi street canyon) and 'a standard 5G channel model' (p. 2), but TR 38.901 is never cited by number. Please confirm q2: generalization without retraining is claimed (p. 1-2) and outdoor and NLOS scenarios are evaluated (p. 3), but the training protocol for those tests is not detailed.
